subject: Literature
title: E.M. Forster's The Machine Stops
description: A short lesson to help you apply E.M. Forster's The Machine Stops.

hook.text: In 1909, E.M. Forster predicted video calls, remote work, and total digital dependency in a twelve-thousand-word story.

buildup.text: Humanity lives in underground pods, communicating through screens, and relies on 'the Machine' for every need.

discovery.text: People have lost the ability to experience anything directly. All knowledge comes through the Machine's mediation.

twist.text: When the Machine finally breaks down, humans have forgotten how to survive without it and civilization collapses.

climax.text: Forster's century-old story reads like a review of modern life, predicting our screen addiction with uncanny precision.

punchline.text: He described Zoom, remote work, and digital life in 1909.

quiz.question: What happens when the Machine breaks down in Forster's story?
options: People quickly adapt and rebuild civilization
Humans have forgotten how to survive without it and civilization collapses
A new, better machine immediately replaces it
